塞奥菲拉克托斯勾勒暴君与合法国王的不同品格与统治，而为两者提及的第一项都是他如何上台。他这样做不是因为描述按时间格式，而是因为这一标准切中其正当性核心。就合法国王而言，他对其地位来源毫不含糊：“全体群众立他为自己的首领。”
en: In accordance with his model of the

Cicero imagined that the early kings of Rome were formally elected by the people, while those who were not sought popular acclamation afterward; in any case, to be legitimate they had to govern on the people’s behalf.

The fundamental logic was well understood in Byzantium. The twelfth-century verse chronicler Konstantinos Manasses has all the Romans gather and vote to abolish the monarchy and institute the consuls at the founding of the Republic.
This is the inverse of the
but perfectly complements it. It was possible under the Komnenoi to believe that the Roman

had such sovereign powers. Beyond such specific instances, however, it was a commonplace in the Mirrors that the foundations of an emperor’s rule lay in popular consent. In the 1080s, Theophylaktos, already or soon to be the archbishop of Bulgaria, addressed a potential heir to the throne in a work which explained that the term
comes from βάσις οὖσα λαοῦ, “the foundation of the people” (you have a
by contrast, “when the entire people make an active contribution to the administration of the
The key difference between a tyrant and a lawful
is that the tyrant does not receive the reins of power from the people but grabs them for himself by force.
The
by contrast, receives power “by the good will of the multitude and the consent of the people.”

Theophylaktos delineates the different characters and reigns of the tyrant and the legitimate king, and the first item that he mentions for each is how he came to power. He does this not because his descriptions have a chronological format but because this criterion cuts to the heart of their legitimacy. In the case of the legitimate king, he leaves no doubt about the source of his position: “the entire multitude makes him its leader.”

zh: 尽管这些文本有趣、或许特异，
拜占庭的人民主权不能靠堆砌指向该方向的引文来确立。毕竟靠引文数量优势证明皇帝的正当性取决于上帝的眷顾、因而拜占庭是神权政体，要容易得多。我们必须从政治行动的模式及其话语表述的结合中推断关于权力与正当性关系的底层前提。我们还须更仔细考察皇帝如何被立、又如何被废——正如他们中如此多者那样。正是在这些事件中我们将找到使人民主权重新活起来的血液。
en: Interesting while these texts are, and perhaps idiosyncratic,

popular sovereignty in Byzantium cannot be established by piling up quotations that gesture in that direction. It would, after all, be much easier to prove through a preponderance of citations that the legitimacy of the emperor was a function of divine favor, and that Byzantium was therefore a theocracy. It is rather from the patterns of political action, in conjunction with their discursive representation, that we must infer underlying assumptions about relations of power and legitimacy. We must also look more closely at how emperors were made and how they were taken down, as so many of them were. It is in these events that we will find the blood with which to reanimate popular sovereignty.

zh: 民众欢呼与皇帝即位
en: Popular Acclamations and Imperial Accession

zh: 在拜占庭要成为罗马人的皇帝，须先被
（即挑选）担任该职，然后由民众
就位。
几乎总是在公众齐声欢呼的仪式上举行：“每一次皇帝任命都应出自即时的民众要求。”
正当性来自对每位皇帝即位的普遍共识——
或
——基本上是西塞罗
定义的君主制变体。
如一份文本所言，“群众鼓掌……所有人一个声音、一个心思：一个名字取悦全体人民”。
相比之下
取决于帝国政治史该时刻的偶然权力事实。它可由在位皇帝为继承人策划，期望在公开仪式上经普遍共识批准。或一支军队向都城进军、其将军自荐为皇位候选人：若他拿下都城几乎必获欢呼（部分因为没有居民支持很难拿下都城）；若没拿下则事情不确定。
或在无继承人或主张者时，选举皇帝的权利通过似乎每次都不同的各种程序委托给政体某要素（通常元老院、或皇后、或一个委员会），但随之产生的候选人仍须获得普遍欢呼。
en: To become emperor of the Romans in Byzantium one had first to be
(i.e., chosen) for the office and then
to it.
almost always took place in a public ceremony of universal acclamation: “every imperial appointment was supposed to issue from an instant popular demand.”
Legitimacy was derived from universal consensus to every emperor’s accession, the
or
basically a monarchical variation of Cicero’s definition of
As one text put it, “the crowds applauded... all had one voice, one mind: one name pleased all the people.”
The

by contrast, depended on the contingent facts of power at that moment in the empire’s political history. It could be orchestrated by a ruling emperor for an heir, in the expectation that it would be ratified by universal consensus at a public ceremony. Or an army would march on the capital and its general presented himself as a candidate for the throne: if he took the City he was almost certain to be acclaimed (in part because it was difficult to take the City without the support of its population); if he did not take the City, the matter was uncertain.

Or, in the absence of an heir or a claimant, the right to elect an emperor was delegated, through a variety of procedures that seem to have differed each time, to some element of the polity (usually the senate, or the empress or a committee), but the ensuing candidate again had to secure universal acclamation.

zh: 这些动作与谋划正是政治的素材。它们不改变这一事实：该过程的结果被视为正当，因为它反映罗马人民的普遍意志。人民很少积极参与皇帝选举，但他们对使即位正当化是必要的。这一关键区分在学术中并非总被作出——学术倾向更关注选举（揭示权力事实）而非公开拥立（通常被视为空洞仪式）。但那一仪式表明权力事实是在人民同意与批准的意识形态内展开的，即便不是人民选择。我们的选举也非全然不同：我们很少看到筹款活动和其他“见面会”——财阀借此预先决定候选人是谁、谁被排除。这些权力事实严格说不民主、违反民主精神。然而它们事后经“自由”选举中的民众投票批准，没有它整个设置就不正当。在拜占庭，如同在古代与现代共和国，人民是政治正当性的最终来源，尽管他们经常把人事选择让给精英集团。
en: These moves and machinations were the stuff of politics. They did not change the fact that the result of this process was regarded as legitimate because it reflected the universal will of the Roman people. The people were rarely active in the election of emperors, but they were necessary to legitimate their accession. This crucial distinction is not always made in the scholarship, which tends to focus more on the election (as revealing the facts of power) than the elevation (which is usually seen as an empty ceremony). But that ceremony reveals that the facts of power played out within an ideology of popular consent and ratification, if not popular choice. Our elections are not altogether different: few of us see the fundraisers and other “meet-and-greets” by which the plutocracy decides in advance who the candidates are going to be and who is excluded. These facts of power are not, strictly speaking, democratic, and violate the spirit of democracy. Yet they are ratified retroactively by a popular vote in “free” elections, without which the whole setup would be illegitimate. In Byzantium, as in ancient and modern republics, the people were the ultimate source of political legitimacy, though they regularly ceded choices of personnel to elite groups.

zh: 罗马人的意志如何被表述为普遍？现代学术（及某些古代与拜占庭史料）使用的公式是：新皇帝须获得“元老院、军队与人民”的支持。
两点限定必要。其一，我们不关心这些要素是否各自在新皇帝挑选中扮演积极角色——尽管有时各自确实如此。它们的主要角色（通常须一致扮演）是使选择正当化或拒绝如此。其二，共识在仪式上被策划的确切方式因即位而异：场合、事件顺序、侧重、人物与集团的突出程度，以及不同史料如何描述。礼仪灵活，组织者有一系列选项与先例可依其特定处境、挑战与口味选择。
我们不应期待统一。报道这些事件的史料亦然。每种以自己的方式列出出席拥立皇帝的仪式的政体要素，试图接近全面但不反映固定公式。元老院、军队、人民的公式不像许多学者想的那样固定。于是以各种组合我们见到对皇室、不同军队单位、宫廷卫队、宫廷官员、最高职官、战车竞赛派系及其代表、集体人民、商人、元老院、“法律”、“整个世界”、牧首与教士的提及。不同史料甚至对同一事件报道不同，列出共和国不同要素参与。
en: How was the will of the Romans represented as universal? The formula used in modern scholarship, and in some ancient and Byzantine sources, is that new emperors had to obtain the support of “the Senate, army, and people.”

Two qualifications are in order. First, we are not concerned with whether each of these elements played an active role in the selection of the new emperor, though at times each of them did. Their main role, which they normally had to play in unison, was to legitimate the choice or refuse to do so. Second, the exact manner in which consensus was orchestrated ceremonially changed from one accession to another, in terms of setting, the order of events, the emphasis, the prominence of persons and groups, and also in how it was described in different sources. The protocol was flexible and the organizers had a range of options and precedents from which to choose based on their particular circumstances, challenges, and tastes.

We should not expect uniformity. This is also true of the sources that report these events. Each lists the elements of the polity that were present at imperial elevations in its own way, trying to approximate comprehensiveness but not reflecting a fixed formula. The formula of senate, army, and people was not quite as fixed as many scholars think. So, in various combinations, we have references to the imperial family, different army units, the palace guard, palace officials, the top magistrates, the racing factions, the representatives of the racing factions, the people collectively, merchants, the senate, “the laws,” “the entire world,” the patriarch, and the clergy. Different sources even reported the same event differently, listing different elements of the republic as participating.

zh: 这有两个后果。其一，我们不能用这些印象式清单追踪各时期使新皇帝正当化的变动“宪制要求”；
毕竟没有正式宪法界定任何这些关系。其二，我们未必能用这些清单追踪拜占庭变动的社会史——假定被点名的集团当时在帝国政治中必定特别突出。
我们的作者不遵循固定宪制公式（那不存在），也未必反映社会关系。汉斯-格奥尔格·贝克（Hans-Georg Beck）事实上正是那些时代错置地试图从史料描述的混乱选举过程中提取正式宪法、并以国家不同“机关”（通常元老院、人民、军队）表述它的史家之一。他对这部宪法及其法律维度的看法过分讲究形式，所描述的机构却只能说已有某些制度特征，且缺乏意识形态理论。
我们的史料各自以自己的方式试图说的是“政体中的所有人”，否则就提政体某要素作为简写（通常元老院、军队或人民）。
en: This has two consequences. First, we cannot use these impressionistic lists to track the changing “constitutional requirements” by which a new emperor was made legitimate in each period;

after all, there was no formal constitution that defined any of these relationships. Second, we cannot necessarily use these lists to track the changing social history of Byzantium, on the assumption that specified groups must have been especially prominent in imperial politics at that time.

Our authors were not following set constitutional formulae, which did not exist, nor were they necessarily reflecting social relations. Hans-Georg Beck was in fact among those historians who anachronistically tried to extract a formal constitution from the messy election processes that our sources describe, and cast it in terms of different “organs” of the state (typically the senate, people, and army). His view of this constitution and its legal dimension was too formal, but only quasi-institutional, and lacked a theory of ideology.

What our sources were trying to do, each in its own way, was to say “everyone in the polity,” or else they mention one element of the polity as a kind of shorthand (usually the senate, the army, or the people).

zh: 当然拜占庭确有社会史。政体不同要素（军队、元老“贵族”、高级教士或贸易集团）在共和国政治经济生活中有或大或小突出的时刻，它们在皇帝立废中的角色或反映这些波动。人民如我们将见通常不在这些时刻带头，尽管其同意对使结果正当化必要。另一项研究将讨论这个拜占庭“罗马人共和国”贵族的性质、以及人民与主导要素（政治、军事或教会）在多大程度上自认属于一个相对未分化的民族群体。这里论点不同：报道特定集团参与这些欢呼的文本不是在暗写社会史。它们通常试图强调新皇帝所享支持的多样性。想法是出席的社会群体越多样，就越能代表共和国的更大范围。史家塞奥菲拉克托斯·西莫卡塔（Theophylaktos Simokattes）告诉我们574年查士丁二世开始失智时，召元老院、高级教士与牧首入宫宣布擢升提比略二世（Tiberios II）为
。查士丁对提比略说：“当你看见这些人在此，你就看见整个
我们必须接受每种史料对事件给出有限视角。其他同时代史料说那次场合除元老院与高级教士外还有共和国其他要素出席，
而更晚史料事后叙述该事件时想当然认为查士丁召了人民、元老院、祭司与职官。
然后为从查士丁下的
升为亲自主政的
，提比略二世很可能后来经人民正式欢呼，尽管史料对此言之甚少。
en: Certainly, Byzantium did have a social history. Different elements of the polity (the army, the senatorial “aristocracy,” the higher clergy, or trade groups) had moments of greater or lesser prominence in the political and economic life of the republic, and their role in the making and unmaking of emperors may have reflected these fluctuations. The people, as we will see, usually did not take the lead at such moments, although their consent was necessary to legitimate the outcome. A separate study will discuss the nature of the aristocracy of this Byzantine “republic of the Romans” and the extent to which the people and the leading elements (political, military, or ecclesiastical) understood themselves as belonging to a relatively undifferentiated national group. The point being made here is different: the texts that report the participation of specific groups at these acclamations are not covertly writing social history. They are usually trying to emphasize the diversity of the support enjoyed by a new emperor. The idea was that a variety of different social groups represented more of the republic. The historian Theophylaktos Simokattes tells us that in 574, when Justin II began to lose his mind, he summoned the senate, top clergy, and patriarch to the palace to announce that he was elevating Tiberios II to the rank of
Addressing Tiberios, Justin said, “As you behold these men here, you behold the entire

We have to accept that each source presents a limited view of events. Other contemporary sources state that additional elements of the republic were present on that occasion than just the senate and top clergy,
and when much later sources narrated the event in hindsight they took it for granted that Justin had summoned the people, senate, priests, and magistrates.
Then, to make the transition from
under Justin to
in his own right, Tiberios II was likely later acclaimed formally by the people, though our sources say little about it.

zh: 如我们在米海尔五世（1042年被人民推翻）处也见，继承人可由在位皇帝或皇后在较“私人”的宫廷仪式中擢升至次于皇帝的尊位（如
），仪式包括职官、高级教士、宫廷卫队单位与人民代表。随后当他们自主掌权时，会在赛马场或其他公开仪式经全体人民欢呼。史料有时只顺带提及该事件，但它不可回避。即便新皇帝或其操盘者不专门为此举办公共仪式，他也必在其皇帝保荐人死后尽快出现在人民面前——无论在葬礼、竞技会或圣索菲亚大教堂。所有公开露面都要求人民欢呼皇帝，不仅新统治开始而且每次。大批民众每次集合以欢呼认可皇帝，都再度确认其统治权；
它“重复了帝国意识形态的约束纽带”。
皇帝
须在与臣民互动时获得普遍认可。当这不发生、当公众舆论情绪转向反对某皇帝时，共和国就进入危机阶段，触发如第5章将讨论的事件（如本章开头考察的米海尔五世倒台）。在政体不受欢迎时期，皇帝可能想避开大群群众，因为一切可能迅速出错。一部分人民可能嘘声嘲骂，而无法预测事件届时如何展开。公开露面可能迅速变成对政体的公投。大多数时候事情顺利，产生史家所称“仪式”。其他时候结果是“历史”。
en: As we saw also with Michael V (who was toppled by the people in 1042), heirs could be elevated by a reigning emperor or empress to a lesser imperial rank (e.g.,

) in a more “private” court ceremony that included magistrates, top clergy, palace guard units, and representatives of the people. Subsequently, when they came into power in their own right, they would be acclaimed by the full people in the hippodrome or some other public ceremony. Our sources sometimes only allude to that event in passing, but it could not be avoided. Even if a new emperor or his handlers did not stage a public ceremony specifically for that purpose, he was bound to appear before the people as soon as his imperial sponsor died, whether at the funeral, the games, or in Hagia Sophia. All public appearances required that the people acclaim the emperor, not just at the start of a new reign but every time. Large crowds gathering to approve of an emperor constituted an ongoing ratification of his right to rule;
it “iterated the binding links of imperial ideology.”
An emperor

had to meet with universal approval whenever he interacted with his subjects. When this did not happen, when the mood of public opinion turned against an emperor, then the republic entered a crisis phase that triggered events such as we will discuss in Chapter 5 (e.g., the fall of Michael V examined at the beginning of this chapter). In times when the regime was unpopular, emperors might want to avoid large crowds because it could all go wrong quickly. A segment of the people might boo and jeer, and there was no way to predict how events might unfold then. Public appearances could quickly become a referendum on the regime. Most of the time things went well, producing what historians call “ceremony.” At other times, the result was “history.”

zh: 我们拥有的拜占庭政治史史料（在有史料的时期）倾向聚焦冲突时刻而非享有公众支持之皇帝的例行欢呼。这就是为何我们关于新皇帝即位的细节很少。碰巧有一份对阿纳斯塔修斯（Anastasios，491年）的记述是详细的。它被保留在10世纪《仪典之书》（
）中，想必作为仍相关的模型。
该记述表明共和原则在这些事件中牢固运作，并补充本章开头考察的米海尔五世倒台的详细记述，两相对照：一则记载一位皇帝的即位，一则记载五百多年后另一位皇帝统治的终结。比较表明都城人民在本书考察的整个时期保留其根本政治权利与意识形态。
en: Our sources for Byzantine political history, in the periods when we have them, tend to focus on moments of conflict rather than the routine acclamations of emperors who enjoyed public support. That is why we have few details about the making of new emperors. We happen to have one account, for Anastasios (in 491), that is detailed. It was retained, presumably as a still-relevant model, in the tenth-century

This account reveals that republican principles were firmly at work in these events, and it complements the detailed accounts of the fall of Michael V that we examined at the beginning of this chapter, forming convenient book-ends at the start and end of two dissimilar reigns, separated by over 500 years. The comparison reveals that the people of the City retained their fundamental political rights and ideology throughout the period examined in this book.

zh: 泽农（Zenon）死的那夜（491年4月9日），元老院、职官与牧首在宫中集会，而人民与士兵在赛马场集结。职官告诉皇后阿里阿德涅（Ariadne）到赛马场向人民讲话，她照做了，与职官和牧首一起。在随后的交流中，民众要求让一位信奉正统教义的罗马人当皇帝（其一暗指当时激烈的神学争论，其二暗指伊苏里亚人泽农的准蛮族族属）。阿里阿德涅告知民众她已指示职官与元老院（注意：不是牧首）挑选一位基督徒罗马男子为下任皇帝，且须有德。她坚持该过程不受友谊、仇恨、别有用心的动机、亲属或任何其他个人因素影响。我们在此清楚看到政体职分与帝国政府如何被非人格化地构想：正如皇帝之选理论上应非人格化地决定，皇帝本人也被期望以同样方式统治。人民趁此机会告诉阿里阿德涅除掉都城长官——一个“贼”——她告诉他们她已有同样打算并任命了新都城长官尤利安诺斯（Ioulianos）（后来因其不受欢迎措施引发暴动而在民众压力下被免职）。
en: On the night that Zenon died (9 April 491), the senate, the magistrates, and the patriarch met in the palace while the people and soldiers assembled in the hippodrome. The magistrates told the empress Ariadne to appear in the hippodrome and address the people, which she did, along with the magistrates and the patriarch. In the ensuing exchange, the populace demanded an emperor who was Orthodox and a Roman (an allusion, in the first place, to the raging theological controversy and, in the second, to the quasi-barbarian ethnicity of the Isaurian Zenon). Ariadne informed the populace that she had already instructed the magistrates and the senate (not the patriarch, we note) to select a Christian Roman man as the next emperor, who would be virtuous. She insists that the process would not be influenced by friendship, hatred, ulterior motives, kinship, or any other personal factor in the selection. We see here clearly how the offices of the polity and the imperial government were conceptualized impersonally: just as the choice of the emperor was, in theory, to be decided impersonally, the emperor himself was expected to rule in the same way. The people take the opportunity now to tell Ariadne to get rid of the prefect of the City, who was a “thief,” and she tells them that she already had the same purpose in mind and appointed a new prefect, Ioulianos (later to be dismissed because of popular pressure when his unpopular measures provoked a riot).

zh: 皇后与职官退入宫中，后者集会商议但无法达成一致。其中一人提议由皇后挑选，她于是选中阿纳斯塔修斯。士兵被派往他家把他带进宫。泽农的葬礼次日举行。再下一天职官与元老要求阿纳斯塔修斯宣誓不对任何人怀怨（即放下私人生活、承担公共角色），
并尽其所能治理

。他被带到赛马场——浓缩一长系列授职仪式——在那里经人民欢呼为奥古斯都。在随后的交流中人民要求他只任命廉正的官员治理，而他强调自己本不愿接受此位、但现在被他们的普遍共识说服。“我并非不知道为所有人的共同安全而置于我肩上的责任负担何等沉重”，并“我恳求全能的上帝：你们将发现我在公共事务（τὰ πράγματα）上如你们如今普遍选举我时（ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ κοινῇ ἐκλογῇ）所期望的那样努力”。双方反复表达希望罗马人如今繁荣。阿纳斯塔修斯然后入内。
en: The empress and magistrates retire into the palace, and the latter meet to deliberate, but they cannot agree. One of them proposes that the selection be made by the empress, and she then selects Anastasios. Soldiers are sent to his house to bring him to the palace. The funeral of Zenon takes place the following day. On the day after that the magistrates and senators demand that Anastasios swear an oath not to hold a grievance against anyone (that is, to set aside his private life and take on a public role),
and that he govern the

to the best of his ability. He is led to the hippodrome where, to condense a long series of investitures, he is acclaimed by the people as Augustus. Among the ensuing exchanges, the people ask that he appoint only pure magistrates to govern while he stresses that he had been unwilling to accept this position but is persuaded now by their universal consensus. “I am not unaware how great a burden of responsibility has been placed upon me for the common safety of all,” and “I entreat God the Almighty that you will find me working as hard at public affairs (τὰ πράγματα) as you had hoped when you universally elected me now (ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ κοινῇ ἐκλογῇ).” Both sides repeatedly express a hope that the Romans will now flourish. Anastasios then goes inside.

zh: 这比随后许多欢呼更有秩序。但它在叙述中未必被粉饰。虽然它保存于礼仪手册，该手册也包括混乱即位的记述，如查士丁一世（Justin I）那次被注明“无序”。
en: This was a more orderly process than many subsequent acclamations. Yet it has not necessarily been whitewashed in the telling. While it is preserved in a ceremonial manual, the latter includes accounts of messy accessions, such as that of Justin I, which is noted as being “disorderly.”

zh: 阿纳斯塔修斯选举的记述揭示职官会议的分歧、也揭示他当时在家。与大多数欢呼（皇帝之选已成既成事实）不同，本例中他无法确知自己会被选中。职官不是假装分歧以便有借口把事交给阿里阿德涅。他们不是橡皮图章批准预定选择。更重要的是该过程铭刻在共和意识形态框架内。阿纳斯塔修斯是被人民与军队欢呼为奥古斯都这一事实
为奥古斯都的；他的统治权奠基在那普遍共识上，过程的每一步都仔细地征得在场民众同意。他宣誓尽责治理政体并承诺为臣民努力工作。他的
作为一种服务形式不可能有其他目的；就此而言皇帝任命与任何其他职官任命无异——后者也须宣誓为政体之善履职。
整个过程中人民提出自己的要求：既意识形态的（这次他们要一个纯罗马人皇帝）也涉及具体人事的（“我们不喜欢这个都城长官；除掉他”）。阿里阿德涅两点都让步。他们还清楚表明阿纳斯塔修斯将被以高道德、政治与宗教标准衡量；我们将看到后来一些臣民认为他不达标。那时他们试图废黜他，但他幸存——不像他许多继任者。人民从未忘记：既然能立皇帝，也能废皇帝。
en: The account of Anastasios’s election reveals the dissention in the council of magistrates, also the fact that he was at home. Unlike most acclamations, where the choice of emperor was a fait accompli, there was no way in this instance that he could have known for certain that he would be selected. The magistrates did not pretend to disagree simply to have a pretext to turn the matter over to Ariadne. They did not rubber-stamp a predetermined choice. More importantly, the process was inscribed within a republican ideological framework. Anastasios was

an Augustus by the fact that the people and the army acclaimed him as such; his right to rule rested on that universal consensus and every step in the process was cleared carefully with the assembled multitudes. He swore an oath to govern the polity conscientiously and promised to work hard on behalf of his subjects. His

as a form of service, could have no other purpose, and to this extent the appointment of an emperor did not differ from the appointment of any other magistrate, who also had to swear an oath to fulfill his duties for the good of the polity.

During the whole process, the people made their own demands, both ideological (they want a purely Roman emperor this time) and relating to specific personnel (“We don’t like the prefect; get rid of him”). Ariadne conceded both points. They also made it clear that Anastasios would be held up to high moral, political, and religious standards, and we will see that he was later found wanting by some of his subjects. When that happened, they tried to depose him, but he survived, unlike many of his successors. The people never forgot that, having made an emperor, they could also unmake him.

zh: 因此皇帝即位事务包含与人民谈判，通常在赛马场。例如导致查士丁一世即位（518年）的“无序”事件中，人民在赛马场集结并欢呼元老院、授权它挑选新皇帝。卫队一个党派试图让自己的候选人获欢呼，但被蓝党（赛马场上一支竞赛战车队的支持者）喝倒彩、向他投石（他后来成为主教）。第二个党派用自己的候选人尝试，结果被第一个党派移除。最后元老院宣布支持查士丁——他为所有人接受。政治或许混乱，但支配它的原则（如一个党派首领所述）无可质疑：“我们的主人身为凡人已经死了。我们现在必须共同商议找出取悦上帝、有利于
的人。”
en: The business of imperial accession, then, entailed negotiation with the people, usually in the hippodrome. For example, in the “disorderly” events that led to the accession of Justin I (518), the people assembled in the hippodrome and acclaimed the senate, authorizing it to select a new emperor. One faction of the guard tried to have its own candidate acclaimed, but he was shouted down by the Blues (the fans of a hippodrome racing team), who threw stones at him (he later became a bishop). A second faction had a go with their own candidate, only to have him removed by the first faction. Finally, the senate declared its support for Justin, who was acceptable to all. The politics may have been messy, but the principle governing it, as stated by the leader of one of the factions, was beyond question: “Our lord, being a man, has died. We must now take counsel in common to find the man who will be pleasing to God and advantageous for the

zh: 如上所述皇帝即位是复杂过程，故试图隔离出拥有正式权力授予皇权的那一个“宪制”要素、或一个人成为皇帝的确切时刻，是有风险的。该问题在早期罗马帝国语境中被更广泛讨论，但这些讨论常常相互错位：一位史家找权力事实、另一位找当时用来使之正当化的意识形态；且不同学者使用不同“意识形态”与“宣传”观念。
无论如何，奥古斯都在其《功业录》（
）中宣称其权力由元老院与人民授予；此后数世纪皇帝经民众集会制定的法律（
）正式被授予职官权力。政治制度履行了体现人民主权的礼仪程序，皇帝声称被人民召掌权。
我们若愿意可把这一切当“虚构”或“宣传”，但也须承认它是根深蒂固的意识形态；即这是拜占庭皇权正当化唯一可接受的框架，并根本塑造了它如何能被使用。晚期古代事情更复杂：神选观念移到前台、成为潜在替代正当性来源。第6章将讨论。
en: As noted above, the accession of an emperor was a complex process, and so efforts to isolate the one “constitutional” element that had the formal power to bestow imperial power, or the precise moment at which a man became emperor, are risky. The question has been discussed more extensively in connection with the early Roman empire, but these discussions are often at cross-purposes, as one historian is looking for the facts of power and another for the ideology that was then used to legitimate them; also, different scholars employ different notions of “ideology” and “propaganda.”
Be that as it may, in his

Augustus proclaimed that his powers were bestowed upon him by the senate and people, and for centuries thereafter emperors were formally invested with magisterial powers by laws enacted in popular assemblies (the
). The political system went through the motions of popular sovereignty, and the emperors claimed to have been called to power by the people.

We can treat all this as “fiction” or “propaganda” if we like, but we must also recognize that it was a deeply embedded ideology; that is, this was the only acceptable framework for the legitimation of imperial power in Byzantium, and it fundamentally shaped how it could be used. Matters became more complicated in late antiquity, when the idea of divine election moved to the foreground and became a potential alternative source for legitimacy. We will discuss this in Chapter 6.

zh: 这里须就“晚期古代”说一句话，因为罗马史家很可能被误导关于这个如今被大量研究的时代对拜占庭形成的意义。具体而言，熟悉元首制（Principate）模型的史家看着3世纪及以后漫游而军事化的皇帝；观察到神选主张上升；被拜占庭学家告知帝国如今有彻底基督教意识形态、“并非真正罗马”；于是合理得出结论：拜占庭（他们假定是晚期古代的产物与延伸）必定也是军事独裁、其“意识形态”是神选。有人甚至仍称它为东方专制。我相反提出：从政治上说，古代晚期这大约二百年，一度偏离了罗马
以人民为根基的规范，故常从它得出的关于“拜占庭”的更广泛结论是扭曲的。约400年宫廷在新罗马重建、及其与民众发展的紧密关系，使我们见证向由文职统治的（罗马）模式的回归与共和原则的强化。这从阿纳斯塔修斯即位记述及我们对后来数世纪君士坦丁堡政治的了解中清楚浮现。反常的是晚期古代——尽管它在过去数十年学术中已显得规范。
en: A word is necessary here on “late antiquity,” because Roman historians are likely to be misled about the significance of this now much-studied era for the formation of Byzantium. Specifically, historians who are familiar with the model of the Principate look at the roaming and militaristic emperors of the third century and afterward; they observe the rise in claims to divine election; are told by Byzantinists that the empire now had a thoroughly Christian ideology and was “not really Roman”; and so reasonably conclude that Byzantium, which they assume was the product and extension of late antiquity, must also have been a military dictatorship whose “ideology” was that of divine election. Some even call it still an oriental despotism. I propose, by contrast, that those roughly 200 years in late antiquity were, politically speaking, a deviation from the populist norms of the Roman

and so the broader conclusions that are often drawn from it about “Byzantium” are distorted. With the reestablishment of the court in New Rome ca. 400 and the tight relationship that it developed with the populace, we witness both a return to civilian (Roman) modes and an intensification of republican principles. This emerges clearly from the account of Anastasios’s accession and from what we know about Constantinopolitan politics in later centuries. It is late antiquity that is aberrant, for all that it has come to seem normative in scholarship of the past decades.

zh: 就帝国政治史而言，我们可把晚期古代定义为3世纪早期
终结与5世纪新罗马共和规范重建之间的时期。此期间皇帝倾向随军漫游、通常由军队挑选与欢呼。但即便这些军人皇帝须与罗马
打交道时，他们也遭遇所谓“准共和行为形式”，
而其军事式欢呼努力保留罗马人民选举的理论——本例中是武装的人民。
行省的四帝共治首都同样旨在促进皇帝与所谓“地方
”的互动，
尽管我们没有关于那些互动的叙事史料。我的目的不是追溯该主题从罗马经“晚期古代”到君士坦丁堡的历史，只是解释君士坦丁堡安定于其模式与秩序后支配政治领域的原则。这正是本研究始于约500年的主要原因。我为拜占庭本部阐述的皇权正当性理论在皇帝率军巡行的阶段同样起作用，只是表现形式因军事环境而改变，作用也受其限制。
en: In terms of the political history of the empire, we could define late antiquity as the period between the end of the

in the early third century and the reestablishment of republican norms at New Rome in the fifth century. During this period, emperors tended to roam with their armies and were usually selected and acclaimed by the armies. But when even these military emperors had to deal with the Roman
they too encountered what have been called “quasi-republican forms of behavior,”
and their military-style acclamations tried hard to preserve the theory of election by the Roman people, the people under arms in this case.
Tetrarchic capitals in the provinces were likewise meant to facilitate interaction between the emperor and what has been labeled the “local

though we have no narrative sources about those interactions. It is not my purpose to trace the history of this theme from Rome to Constantinople through “late antiquity,” only to explain the principles governing the political sphere once Constantinople had settled into its modes and orders. That is the main reason why this study begins with ca. 500. The theory of imperial legitimacy that I have laid out for Byzantium proper was also operative during the phase of the itinerant armies, but it was inflected and limited in specifically military ways.

zh: 就我们的时期（不妨说阿纳斯塔修斯之后）而言，似乎清楚：
皇帝只有获得罗马人民普遍同意才被视为正当。
反面也真：民众非难能废黜皇帝。那些时刻所有即位与权力的附属物——皇冠、服饰、誓言、圣物与圣像、神授主张——相对
的权力与权利都一文不值。我们将回到“反欢呼”——即位的反面。这里我想呈现一批关乎拜占庭人如何思考正当性（尤其当须作选择时）的段落样本。他们尽可能让上帝参与，但正当性的基岩是共和的。某些事件中，有人显然借人民拥戴的原则掩饰派系政变。这远非反对我论点的证据，事实上是对其最强可能的确认：拜占庭的权力再分配

children: 仅凭人民拥戴这一理由就取得正当性

zh: ，而不论各例中的权力事实。这正是“意识形态”所起的作用。
en: For our period (let us say, after Anastasios), it seems clear that
an emperor was held to be legitimate only when he had received the universal consent of the Roman people.

The converse was also true: popular disapprobation could unmake an emperor. At such moments all the associated accoutrements of accession and power, including crowns, vestments, oaths, relics and icons, and claims to divine sanction, were worthless compared to the power and rights of the

We will come back to “deacclamation,” the flip-side of accession. Here I want to present a sampling of passages that bear on the issue of how the Byzantines thought of legitimacy, especially when there was a choice to be made. They tried, where possible, to keep God involved, but the bedrock of legitimacy was republican. In some of these incidents, populist principles were clearly being invoked to cover up a coup by a faction. Far from being evidence against my argument, this is in fact the strongest possible confirmation for it: the reassignment of power in Byzantium
regardless of the facts of power in each case. This is what an “ideology” does.

zh: • 565年查士丁尼死时，元老们接近查士丁（二世），据科里普斯（Corippus）以这些话对他致辞：“当您父亲［实为其叔］在世时，人民知道罗马帝国靠您的谋略与努力维系，我们与人民一致。”
元老们（或科里普斯）觉得必须说这些话，这一事实相对人民在挑选本身中有限发言权而言更显重要。元老们拿这番话为拥立辩护，提出的请求当然经普遍欢呼确认。
en: • When Justinian died in 565, the Senators approached Justin and, according to Corippus, addressed him with these words: “While life remained in your father [actually his uncle], the people knew that the Roman empire was upheld by your counsels, and your efforts, and we agree with the people.”

The fact that the Senators, or Corippus, felt compelled to speak these words is all the more significant in proportion to the people’s limited say in the selection itself. The Senators’ rationalizing plea was, of course, confirmed by universal acclamation.

zh: • 963年罗曼努斯二世死时，继位者是其未成年儿子巴西尔二世与君士坦丁八世。那时将军尼基弗鲁斯·福卡斯（Nikephoros Phokas）凯旋回君士坦丁堡。因惧宦官约瑟夫·布林加斯（Ioseph Bringas）谋害其命，尼基弗鲁斯接近牧首波利埃夫克托斯（Polyeuktos），后者召元老院入宫并除其他外如此劝告：“既然我们是罗马人、依神命规范生活，我们应维护皇帝罗曼努斯的幼子……因为他们由我们与全体人民宣布为皇帝。”
他提议尼基弗鲁斯掌军，但仅在他“被誓言约束不谋划任何不利于国家与元老院之事”后。
en: • When Romanos II died in 963, he was succeeded by his sons Basileios II and Konstantinos VIII, who were minors. At that time, the general Nikephoros Phokas returned to Constantinople in triumph. Fearing plots against his life by the eunuch Ioseph Bringas, Nikephoros approached the patriarch Polyeuktos, who summoned the senate to the palace and, among other things, advised them as follows: “Since we are Romans, and regulate our lives according to divine commands, we should maintain the young children of the emperor Romanos... inasmuch as they were proclaimed emperors by us and all the people.”
He proposed that Nikephoros be placed in charge of the army but only after “he was bound with oaths that he would not plan anything undesirable against the state and the Senate.”

zh: • 普塞洛斯叙述1057年米海尔六世与叛将伊萨克·科穆宁（Isaakios Komnenos）斗争中牧首米海尔·凯鲁拉里奥斯（Michael Keroularios）的角色时说，牧首基本无力改变结果：“若他支持仅形式上的皇帝［米海尔］、抵抗已掌权者［伊萨克］，他仍不能阻止后者成为皇帝，因为后者为全体人民所爱（ὅλῳ τῷ πλήθει ποθούμενον）。”
我们从史料知凯鲁拉里奥斯向米海尔六世发出退位命令，“因为这是群众所要求的”。
普塞洛斯然后明确说由此“叛乱
转化为合法权力
en: • In recounting the role of the patriarch Michael Keroularios in the struggle between Michael VI and the rebel Isaakios Komnenos in 1057, Psellos says that the patriarch was basically powerless to change the outcome: “If he had supported him who was only formally emperor [Michael], resisting the one who already had power in his hands [Isaakios], he would still not have blocked the latter from becoming emperor, as he was beloved by the entire people (ὅλῳ τῷ πλήθει ποθούμενον).”
We know from historical sources that Keroularios sent Michael VI the command to step down “because this was what the multitude were demanding.”
Psellos then explicitly says that thereby “the rebellion
was transformed into a lawful power

zh: • 罗曼努斯四世·第欧根尼（Romanos IV Diogenes）1071年在曼齐克特（Mantzikert）战役被塞尔柱人俘获。短暂囚禁后苏丹放他走，但君士坦丁堡的杜卡斯（Doukas）党派夺权。“第欧根尼行至阿尔美尼亚科伊（Armeniakoi）军区，在那里得知关于自己的消息：即他已被都城人民与宫廷宣布废黜。”
所有人都明白这是宫廷政变，但政变除非被表述为民众决定否则无可能被视为正当。
en: • Romanos IV Diogenes was captured by the Seljuks at the battle of Mantzikert in 1071. After a brief captivity, the sultan let him go, but the Doukas faction in Constantinople seized power. “Diogenes proceeded as far as the theme of the Armeniakoi where he learned the news about himself, namely, that he had been declared deposed by the people of the City and the palace.”
Everyone understood that this was a palace coup, but a coup had no chance of being regarded as legitimate unless it was presented as a popular decision.

zh: • 1195年伊萨克二世·安格洛斯（Isaakios II Angelos）被其兄弟阿莱克修斯三世废黜。“
的职官已欢呼他，其入城已由妻子欧芙罗叙涅（Euphrosyne）预先准备。至于元老院，至少一部分欣然接受既成事实。当
听到宣布时并未起事：从一开始所有人都平静并为消息鼓掌，既不抗议也不因军队剥夺他们任命皇帝的习惯权利而燃起义愤。”
这段不言自明。尤其揭示性的是其作者尼基塔斯·科尼亚特斯（Niketas Choniates）鄙视君士坦丁堡人民，若非当时普遍理解的真理他不会这样写。
en: • In 1195, Isaakios II Angelos was deposed by his brother Alexios III. “The magistrates of the
had already acclaimed him, and his entrance had been prepared in advance by his wife Euphrosyne. As for the Senate, at least a part of it happily accepted what had happened. When the

heard the announcement, they engaged in no seditious behavior: from the start all of them were calm and applauded the news, neither protesting nor becoming inflamed with righteous anger at the fact that the army had removed from them their customary right to appoint the emperor.”

This passage speaks for itself. It is especially revealing in that its author, Niketas Choniates, was contemptuous of the people of Constantinople and would not have written this were it not a generally understood truth in his time.

zh: 我补充一则关于842年米海尔三世继位的报道，尽管它不太可能如其报道方式那样符合事实。主角曼努埃尔（Manuel）可能早已去世，其传记作者似乎出于自身原因延长他的寿命、让他在继位中当主角以展示其受欢迎。这是一个人民被表述为无意于让在位的阿莫里亚（Amorian）王朝继续掌权的案例。
en: I add a report regarding the succession of Michael III in 842, though it is unlikely to be factual in the way in which it is reported. The leading character, Manuel, had possibly already died, and his biographers seem to have extended his life for their own reasons and made him a star in the succession to showcase his popularity. This was a case where the people are presented as disinclined to extend the career of the ruling (Amorian) dynasty.

zh: • 曼努埃尔在赛马场召集人民与士兵，提醒他们自己先前对他们的恩惠后，要求他们宣誓照他所求去做。他们希望他即将自荐皇位，于是照做。他然后宣布米海尔三世与塞奥多拉（其母）为皇帝。“他们大失所望……但服从他的命令，于是继位得到确保。”
en: • Manuel gathered the people and the soldiers in the hippodrome and, after reminding them of his previous benefactions to them, asked them to swear an oath that they would do as he asked. They hoped that he was about to propose himself for the throne, and so did what he asked. He then proclaimed Michael III and Theodora (his mother) as emperors. “They were greatly disappointed... but obeyed his command, and so the succession was ensured.”

zh: 这个故事在历史文本中流传，意味着它对目睹过其他权力转移的读者群是可信的，且鉴于我们已见其中没有不可能之物。第5章将讨论宫廷就继位与人民谈判的实例。关于曼努埃尔的故事之所以成立，是因为它基于拜占庭政治的一个根本真理：在潜在不稳定时刻，受人民欢迎是最关键因素。曼努埃尔本可只凭民众的拥戴就登上皇位，因为
有权以欢呼拥立他。反过来王朝不能把民众支持视为当然，而须甚至通过此类伎俩从人民求得共识。这清楚向我们表明谁
正当化权力、谁
它。
en: This story circulated in historical texts, which means that it was plausible to a readership that had witnessed other transitions of power, and there is nothing in it that is impossible given what we have seen already. In Chapter 5, we will discuss instances when the palace negotiated with the people regarding the succession. The story about Manuel works because it is based on a cardinal truth of Byzantine politics: popularity with the people was the most crucial factor in moments of potential instability. Manuel could have taken the throne for himself through his sheer popularity with a
that was empowered to acclaim him. Conversely, the dynasty could not take popular support for granted and had to elicit consensus from the people even through such tricks. This shows us clearly who
legitimating power and who
it.

zh: 既然我们暂不受历史性约束，也可提及6世纪《尤利安传奇》（
），以叙利亚语写于埃德萨（Edessa）。它是关于皇帝尤利安与约维安（Jovian）的传奇。虽然其中很少历史、大多数情节为文学效果夸张，但其中之一关乎潜在皇帝试图通过民众欢呼获皇位。“尤利安前往罗马接受欢呼，但当他拒绝市民所求的宗教宽容并囚禁城市精英时被市民拒绝。”
他然后去君士坦丁堡，在那里遭一个马克西穆斯（Maximos）反对，后者告诉同胞拒绝他并试图刺杀他但失败。“马克西穆斯的榜样没有说服君士坦丁堡居民，因为［尤利安］在那里获欢呼并‘被称为罗马人的国王’。”
文本似乎对君士坦丁堡有偏见，因为只有罗马的欢呼才使人成为真正皇帝；然而它“强调罗马权威的契约性质”。
一个角色劝皇帝不应走出法律，否则会成为暴君。
en: While we are for the moment not constrained by historicity, we may mention also the sixth-century

written in Syriac in Edessa. It is a romance about the emperors Julian and Jovian. While little in it is historical and most of its storylines are exaggerated for literary effect, one of them concerns the attempts by would-be emperors to gain the throne through popular acclamation. “Julian proceeds to Rome to receive his acclamation, but is refused by the citizens when he denies the religious toleration they request and imprisons the elites of the city.”

He then goes to Constantinople, where he is opposed by one Maximos, who tells his fellow citizens to refuse him and tries to assassinate him, but fails. “Maximos’ example does not convince the inhabitants of Constantinople, since [Julian] is acclaimed there and ‘called the king of the Romans.’ ”
The text seems to have a bias against Constantinople, as only acclamation in Rome makes one a proper emperor; nevertheless, it “emphasizes the contractual nature of Roman authority.”
One character advises the emperor that he should not step outside the law because he would then become a tyrant.

zh: 拜占庭史料指称正式政治同意行为最常用的词是 ψῆφος，也可译为“投票”。以下是帕卡图斯（Pacatus）表达使皇帝正当之共识的假设场景——本例中是狄奥多西一世：
en: The most common term by which Byzantine sources refer to a formal act of political assent is ψῆφος, which can also be translated as a “vote.” Here is the hypothetical scenario by which Pacatus expressed the consensus that made an emperor legitimate, in this case Theodosius I:

zh: 让我们想象我们在某种世界集会上询问：谁应承担如此重担、在
蹒跚时掌管其命运。难道
［即狄奥多西］不会被所有人在部落大会和百人团大会上［如今已废的共和国投票集会］的一切投票选中吗？
en: Let us imagine that we are enquiring in some kind of world assembly about which man should shoulder such a burden and take charge of the destiny of the
as it faltered. Would not
[i.e., Theodosius] be chosen by all the votes of all men in tribes and centuries [the now obsolete Republican voting assemblies]?

zh: 5世纪中期后，这种普遍集会的意象不再是假设——至少在君士坦丁堡，其人口大部分（有时几十万人）出来在皇帝欢呼中“投票”。后期史料中有许多“选举”语言的例子，暗指古代投票集会。
它如此根深蒂固，甚至被用来描述阴谋如何孕育——即当史料不敌视该阴谋时。事实上就连参与密谋的人要使自己相信此事正当，也
用选立皇帝的语言来说明它，因为阴谋只是造就（希望是）新皇帝过程中的一步。
除民意外无固定参照点，共和国政治场域分裂为实际皇帝与潜在皇帝，权力平衡依历史变幻在两者间移动——其中受人民欢迎是关键因素。第5章将描述这一等式把所有人（统治者与臣民皆然）置于的紧张处境。
en: After the mid-fifth century, this image of a universal assembly would not have been hypothetical, at least in Constantinople, most of whose population, a few hundred thousand people at times, turned out to “vote” in the imperial acclamations. There are many examples of the language of “election” in the later sources, alluding to the ancient voting assemblies.
It was so ingrained that it was even used to describe how conspiracies were hatched, that is, when the source is not hostile to the conspiracy. In fact, a conspiracy
to be cast in the language of imperial election in order to be presented as legitimate even to itself, for a conspiracy was but a step in the making of what would hopefully be a new emperor.

With no fixed points of reference other than popular will, the political field of the republic was split between actual emperors and potential emperors, the balance of power shifting between them according to the vagaries of history, among which their popularity with the people was a key factor. Chapter 5 will describe the tense situation in which this equation placed everyone, rulers and subjects alike.

zh: 正是这一共和正当化图式阻止了王朝模型的正式确立。虽然学术普遍错过共和方面，但人们充分理解不存在正当的王朝皇位主张：“皇帝职分从未在法律上世袭……：理论上总是、有时实践上，帝国是选举的。”
已获事实世袭继位的政体代言人仍投射贤能政治与人民选择的意识形态。
世袭“权利”基本只是可用来支持候选资格的众多论据之一——这一条件排除把它视为世袭君主制。
实践上尚未失去民众认可的皇帝可以安排拥立自己的继承人，但这是“对个人命运不可预测的追求、把个人冒险延伸至家庭”。
临时王朝可被允许，但舆论和民众干预也应能使它们终结。外国观察者评论拜占庭这种王朝不稳定及皇帝对皇位把握之脆弱。阿拉伯作家评论罗马人中没有世袭权利或继位规则、弱皇帝会被废。
一位7至8世纪的中国旅行者注意到罗马人选最有能力者为王、但若失败则废之；9世纪一个可萨人奇怪他们为何从不同家族选皇帝。
en: It was this republican schema of legitimation that prevented the formal establishment of a dynastic model. Though scholarship has generally missed the republican aspect, it is well understood that there was no rightful dynastic claim to the throne: “The imperial office never became legally hereditary...: in theory always, and on occasion in practice, the empire was elective.”
Spokesmen for regimes that had attained de facto dynastic succession still projected an ideology of meritocracy and popular choice.
Hereditary “right” was basically only one among many arguments that could be used to support a candidacy, a condition that precludes this from being considered a hereditary monarchy.

In practice, an emperor who was not unpopular could arrange for the elevation of his heir, but this was “the unpredictable pursuit of an individual destiny, an extension to the family of a personal adventure.”

Temporary dynasties could be permitted, but they should also be terminated by popular opinion and interventions. Foreign observers commented on this dynastic instability in Byzantium and the tenuous hold that emperors had on the throne. Arab writers commented that there was no hereditary right among the Romans or rule for the succession and that weak emperors would be deposed.

A Chinese traveler of the seventh to eighth century noted that Romans chose the most capable man as their king but deposed him if he failed, and a Khazar in the ninth century wondered why they chose emperors from different families.

zh: 最有趣的外国证据见于 ibn Shahram 981–982年出使巴西尔二世及其宫廷的记述。他的主人——巴格达的布韦希（Buyids）——正庇护战败的拜占庭叛将巴尔达斯 ·斯克勒罗斯（Bardas Skleros）。皇帝正谈判其引渡，但也惧自己的头号将军巴尔达斯·福卡斯（Bardas Phokas）——后者刚击败斯克勒罗斯。我们有相当详细的 ibn Shahram 与宫廷所有要人会面的记述。某刻布韦希大使告诉皇帝：“［罗马］国家的延续不意味着您［个人］的继续存在，因为鲁米（Rumi）人民对谁做他们的皇帝漠不关心。”不幸原阿拉伯文本此处似乎有讹，故这部分是重构。年轻皇帝在讨论稍后回到此点，承认自己须谨慎行事：“我无力抵抗罗马人这个整体，他们可能视我为背叛者与毁灭者。”
因此若我们相信这份其他方面可靠的报道，我们这里拥有的终究不是“外国”证词，而是一位拜占庭皇帝对自己
脆弱性的承认。它与我们能从拜占庭证据推断的吻合。
en: The most interesting foreign evidence is found in the account of ibn Shahram’s embassy to Basileios II and his court in 981–982. His masters, the Buyids in Baghdad, were sheltering the defeated Byzantine rebel Bardas Skleros. The emperor was negotiating over his extradiction, but was also afraid of his own top general, Bardas Phokas, who had just defeated Skleros. We have a fairly detailed account of ibn Shahram’s meetings with all the powerful men at the court. At one point the Buyid ambassador tells the emperor that “the continuance of the [Roman] state does not imply your [personal] continued existence, for the Rumi people are indifferent as to who is the emperor over them.” Unfortunately, the original Arabic text seems to be corrupt at this point, so this is partially a reconstruction. The young emperor returns to this point later in the discussion, when he admits that he has to tread carefully: “It is not in my power to resist the general body [that is, of the Romans], which might regard me as their betrayer and undoer.”
Therefore, if we believe this otherwise reliable report, what we have here is not “foreign” testimony after all, but a Byzantine emperor’s admission of his own
vulnerability. It matches what we can infer from the Byzantine evidence.

zh: 王朝继位在拜占庭事实上比这些证词暗示的更常见。但我们不应把王朝继位视为与人民分配或再分配权力的权利对立——正如我们在也有政治王朝的现代共和国不那样看。许多情况下王朝的存续是由于人民干预以在面对将废除它（或许为设立自己王朝）的篡位者或闯入者时拯救它。1042年反对米海尔五世的民众起义就是一例；君士坦丁七世及其孙巴西尔二世与君士坦丁八世部分受民众支持保护、免受暂时夺权强人的野心。
en: Dynastic succession was in fact more common in Byzantium than these testimonies suggest. But we should not view dynastic succession as antithetical to the people’s right to assign or reassign power, any more than we do in modern republics that also have political dynasties. In many cases, the survival of a dynasty was due to the people’s intervention to save it in the face of usurpers or interlopers who would abolish it (perhaps to institute their own). The popular uprising against Michael V in 1042 was an instance of this, and Konstantinos VII and his grandchildren Basileios II and Konstantinos VIII were partially protected by popular support from the ambitions of strongmen who temporarily seized the throne.

zh: 所有这些现象基于一个事实：继位不是法律问题而是政治问题。它不能由法律事实决定，因为它不是皇帝以其立法者身份有权决定之事。权力分配是整个
的事。毕竟法律条文可被人民在骚动中拒绝、也可被皇帝专断命令改变。换言之继位法易受拜占庭政体易患的两种例外状态影响——即皇帝与人民的法外行动。于是我们回到卢梭完美反映拜占庭规范的共和主权观：“当人民设立世袭政府——无论一家之君主制或一阶层之贵族制——这不是它订立的契约；而是它给行政的临时形式，直到它乐意另作安排之时。”
en: All these phenomena were based on one fact: the succession was not a legal issue; it was a political one. It could not be decided by legal fact because it was not something the emperor was authorized to decide in his capacity as legislator. The assignment of power was a matter for the entire

Legal enactments, after all, could be rejected by the people in a tumult, and they could be altered by imperial fiat. In other words, a succession law was vulnerable to both of the two states of exception to which the Byzantine polity was prone, namely, to extralegal acts by both the emperor and the people. We return, then, to Rousseau’s view of republican sovereignty which perfectly reflects Byzantine norms: “When it happens that the people institutes a hereditary government, either monarchical in one family, or aristocratic in one order of citizens, this is not an engagement it enters into; it is a provisional form it gives to the administration, until such time as it pleases to order it differently.”

zh: 巴列奥略（Palaiologos）家族在共和国垂死之日登上拜占庭皇位，招致知识分子批评——他们“认为皇帝担任的是一个由选举产生的公职，在位王朝却不正当地把它变成了世袭职位”。
en: The establishment of the Palaiologos family on the throne of Byzantium in the dying days of the republic drew criticism from intellectuals who “viewed the emperor as the holder of an elective public office which the current dynasty had illegitimately turned into a hereditary one.”

zh: 现在有充分理由得出结论：拜占庭政治场域在很大程度上由一种明显罗马而共和的意识形态定义。再不能轻蔑地说所有这些罗马观念仅“在好古与残余意义上”存活。
它们非常活跃。
属于

属于共和国所有成员包括人民。皇帝唯一职责是为政体劳作，他在道德与政治上对臣民负责。人民在决定谁被推到他们面前作为皇位候选人上或许发言权不大，但其同意对其即位与统治正当绝对必要。没有任何权威来源能在此事上压倒人民意志。他们如克利夫·安多（Cliff Ando）所称，是“
的股东、作为一个整体，在国家中仍享有主权”。
en: There are now sufficient grounds to conclude that the Byzantine political sphere was defined in large part by a distinctly Roman and republican ideology. It is no longer possible to say dismissively that all these Roman notions survived only “in an antiquarian and vestigial sense.”
They were very much alive. The
belonged to the
not to the person who happened to occupy the throne, and the

belonged to all members of the republic, including the people. The emperor’s sole responsibility was to labor on behalf of the polity, and he was morally and politically accountable to his subjects. The people may not have had much say in determining who was thrust before them as a candidate for the throne, but their consent was absolutely necessary for his accession and reign to be legitimate. There was no source of authority that could override the will of the people in this matter. They were, as Cliff Ando called them, the “shareholders in the
and in their corporate capacity still sovereign in the state.”

zh: 皇权正当性不仅有民众根源，而且依人民持续好感为条件。公众舆论如第5章将见，即便已在即位仪式正式批准某皇帝也不能视为当然；须持续培育。在这方面拜占庭与东方专制或神授君权恰相反。当我们考虑失人民宠之皇帝的命运时这将清楚浮现。他们的遭遇表明这种共和主义不是虚构、或仅是君主制为动员民众支持而部署的宣传。它对应人们相信在其权利与权力之内者。民众干预插曲“表明君士坦丁堡社会所有阶层多么清楚自己在皇帝立废中的宪制角色——也知道他们能够决定的不只是皇帝的立废”。
没有皇帝或作者否认罗马人民集体意志有权以此方式行使——即便它经常而血腥地如此做。
en: Not only did imperial legitimacy have popular roots, it was contingent upon the people’s continued good will. Popular opinion, as we will see in Chapter 5, could not be taken for granted even when it had formally approved an emperor at a ceremony of accession; it had to be cultivated continuously. In this respect, Byzantium was the exact opposite of an oriental despotism or a monarchy by divine right. This will emerge clearly when we consider the fate of emperors who lost the people’s favor. What happened to them demonstrates that this republicanism was not a fiction or merely propaganda deployed by the monarchy to mobilize popular support. It corresponded to what people believed was within their rights and power. Episodes of popular intervention “illustrate how conscious all sections of Constantinopolitan society were of their constitutional role in the making and unmaking of emperors, and not just of emperors.”
No emperor or author ever denied that the collective will of the Roman people had the right to exert itself in this way, even when it was doing so regularly and bloodily.

zh: 事实上人民在政治场域的角色比迄今论证所示更大。论证只表明人民在皇帝擢升、有时废黜中扮演关键角色。第5章我将论证：人民在几乎所有时候都是拜占庭共和国政治生活的首要因素：皇帝须培育公众舆论并保持在己侧，因为一旦它开始从其掌握中滑落（这经常发生），就有许多在场对手会利用它把自己抬上皇位。就这个意义而言，拜占庭政治一直由民众参与。任何人能否坐稳皇位，都取决于舆论。这比神恩的修辞虚构更能解释拜占庭政治史呈现的图景。
en: In fact, the popular role in the political sphere was even greater than has been indicated by the argument presented so far. The argument has shown only that the people played a crucial role in the elevation and sometimes the deposition of an emperor. I will argue in Chapter 5 that the people were at almost all times a foremost factor in the political life of the Byzantine republic: the emperor had to cultivate public opinion and keep it on his side, because the moment it began to slip from his grasp, which happened often, there were many rivals present who would use it to raise themselves to the throne. In this sense, politics in Byzantium was always popular. One’s hold on the throne was always a function of public opinion. This explains more about the picture that Byzantine political history presents than does the rhetorical fiction of divine favor.

zh: 没有一种通行的理论把权力视为绝对。其共和框架与其说
权力行使（如许多史家今天声称），不如说实际
；它设定人民准备接受政治中所发生之事的条件，正是这给权力行使施加限制。神权修辞的上层建筑正是奠基于此——如我们将见不是作为替代而是作为伙伴：其目的是对抗皇帝面对“公众舆论”的易变与至上、以及缺乏任何绝对政治正当性来源时的极端脆弱性，因为拜占庭政治场域总是可谈判的。我们现在转向这一方面的历史维度。
en: Power was never theorized as absolute. Its republican framework did not so much
the exercise of power, as many historians claim today, as it actually

it set the conditions under which the people were prepared to accept what was happening politically, and this is what imposed restrictions on the exercise of power. It was upon this basis that the superstructure of theocratic rhetoric was imposed, not as an alternative, as we will see, but as a partner: its purpose was to counter the extreme vulnerability of the emperor in the face of the volatility and supremacy of “public opinion” and the absence of any absolute source of political legitimacy, for the political sphere of Byzantium was always negotiable. It is to this aspect, in its historical dimension, that we now turn.

en: Vryonis, “Byzantine ΔΗΜΟΚΡΑΤΙΑ,” especially 302. Vryonis generally blurs the distinction between the guilds and the populace in 1042, but in fact the latter turned against the former in the forum of Constantine, and the sources are unanimous and clear that the entire populace was involved. Charanis, “The Role of the People,” 69–70, believes that “the people” did not mean everyone but some subsection (the merchants and some others), but he is not clear as to which section he means and why he thinks so. None of the sources authorize such qualifications. Hendy,

572–580, does not take into consideration the increase in the number of sources for this period and makes too much of the low birth of certain imperial associates (which had always been a feature of imperial politics); see also Angold, “The Byzantine State,” 24–26; and Cheynet, “La colère du peuple,” which offers a survey but does not regard these disturbances as primarily political. Garland, “Political Power and the Populace,” offers another survey, and questions the “guilds” interpretation (46), but accepts the idea of eleventh- and twelfth-century exceptionalism. Krallis, “ ‘Democratic’ Action,” refers to “the rise of the urban strata” as a new phenomenon. Shepard, “Aspects of Moral Leadership,” 11, refers to the events as the exception rather than the norm but concedes the lack of detailed sources for earlier periods (13). For earlier periods the populist case had been made by Diehl, “Le sénat et le peuple,” but those events are again treated as exceptions by Angold, “The Byzantine Political Process,” 7 (“Popular participation in the political process was thereafter marginal”). See also Syros, “Between Chimera and Charybdis,” 454: “the people’s role in Byzantine politics was often nothing more than cosmetic.” Cameron,
